Lemma
[orthogonal Bianchi decomposition] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0108, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0109, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0110 ↗ def:chow-ii-bianchi-map 1. ch11:11.11\group Algebraic Curvature Operators The restriction of $b$ to $S^2(\Lambda ^2E)$ is a self-adjoint projection onto $\Lambda ^4E$. Consequently \[ S^2(\Lambda ^2E)=\mathcal A_n\oplus \Lambda ^4E \] orthogonally.
Proof

\sketch The pair symmetries of a member of $S^2(\Lambda ^2E)$ show directly that $b(R)$ is alternating in all four entries. If $R$ is already a four-form, cyclic permutation of its first three entries has positive sign, so $b(R)=R$. Finally, reindexing the finite orthonormal-basis sum defining the tensor inner product gives $\langle b(R),S\rangle =\langle R,b(S)\rangle $. Thus $b$ is a self-adjoint projection, and its kernel and image are the asserted orthogonal summands.

□
